messages:
julie_support: Heads-up — OrbitPay (Dedicated) just escalated: export job failed and they report missing audit entries for ~2026-02-12 03:40–03:57 UTC. Ticket INC-12489. Customer says some entries return 'decrypt failed / key not found'. Can @marco_sec triage? @sarah_legal FYI.

marco_sec: On it. Can you paste the export error lines and which region/cluster? Also need key IDs / aliases from the logs.

julie_support: Stack snippet from their export (sanitized):
```
2026-02-12T03:45:12Z ERROR export: decrypt failed: kms:Decrypt failed: key not found (key: projects/keys/k-20260212-1)
2026-02-12T03:46:03Z ERROR export: decrypt failed: kms:Decrypt failed: key not found (key: projects/keys/k-20260212-1)
```
Region: us-west-2. Cluster: dedicated-prod-3. Customer ran an export job for audit logs between 03:30–04:00 UTC and reports ~40 missing entries.

aj_infra: We rotated a secondary KMS key at 2026-02-12T03:42:00Z as part of cert rollover. Primary key alias `redwood/kms-prod` remained. Not aware of export failures at the time. I'll pull rotation logs.

marco_sec: Quick note: are we sure it's HSM-backed key material? OrbitPay is on Dedicated with HSM-backed key policy; if replication to backup HSM failed, decryption could return key-not-found to downstream.

rachel_cs: Customer is alarmed — they asked if this is a data-loss event and whether regulators need notifying. They're blocking until we provide a clear ETA.

sarah_legal: Don't craft final customer wording yet. We need to confirm: 1) whether the affected entries are unrecoverable or just temporarily inaccessible, 2) if any personal data was exfiltrated (seems unlikely from logs), 3) whether this meets PII breach criteria. Keep me looped. If it's potentially a breach, we have to evaluate GDPR 72-hour rules.

marco_sec: Preliminary triage: export job failures spike between 03:41:30–03:58:10 UTC. Count: 42 failed decrypts referencing key alias `k-20260212-1`. From our rotation logs, key material was updated on the primary but the backup HSM did not accept the replication payload due to a vendor replication error (we see error code `HSM-REPL-503`).

aj_infra: I opened vendor support ticket VEND-8821 at 04:10 UTC and engaged them on-call. They confirmed a replication bug and provided a recovery procedure that requires a vendor-assisted key material re-propagation from HSM snapshots. Estimated time-to-recover for affected entries: 8–12 hours once vendor begins full re-propagation.

julie_support: Ok — so we can recover? Do we need customer action or will their export succeed after you re-propagate?

marco_sec: In most cases recovery is possible; decrypt will succeed once the key material is present in the backup HSM. However, the customer export jobs that executed during the gap will need to be re-run or we can re-run their job server-side if they want. We should confirm whether any audit entries were overwritten or lost — unlikely because logs are append-only; this is an accessibility issue.

rachel_cs: OrbitPay wants a clear timeline and an initial customer-safe message. They also asked if this will impact billing or SLO credits.

tom_product: Flagging possible SLO breach — we need to check retention/access SLO for Dedicated. If we missed an availability SLO, credits/process need to be evaluated.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-12489 - KMS key replication gap affecting audit export -> severity P2.

sarah_legal: Draft guidance: send a brief message now saying: we're aware, investigating, no evidence of data exfiltration so far, ETA for more info: 8–12 hours, will follow up with remediation steps. Avoid stating 'data loss' until infra confirms. Keep me copied on any customer comms.

aj_infra: Vendor has started snapshot re-propagation at 04:45 UTC per VEND-8821 notes; they estimate 6–10 hours now. I've attached vendor case link (internal): https://vendor.internal/cases/VEND-8821 (internal).

marco_sec: Action items: 1) aj_infra to coordinate vendor re-propagation and post status updates (owner). 2) infra to run a dry-run re-decrypt against a snapshot and confirm recoverability (aj_infra + marco_sec). 3) cs to send initial customer comms per legal template (rachel_cs). 4) product to assess SLO impact and credit exposure (tom_product). 5) security to produce a short scope doc for legal (marco_sec).

julie_support: I'll tell OrbitPay we're investigating and that we expect an update within 8–12 hours per vendor ETA. Will cc legal and security.

marco_sec: I'll prepare the scope doc with the list of affected keys/entries and the exact time window by EOD. If recovery fails for any subset, we'll escalate severity and start regulator assessment.

sarah_legal: Thanks. Keep comms conservative. If recovery completes, prepare a short postmortem and customer timeline.

rachel_cs: Sending initial note now. I'll attach the contact to the ticket and mark the account priority as P1 until resolved.

marco_sec: Noted. Will update when vendor confirms full re-propagation.

julie_support: INC-12489 updated with vendor ticket and customer note.

marco_sec: (final quick update) vendor confirmed full propagation at 11:10 UTC and we've re-run a validation job — all 42 entries now decrypt locally. We'll coordinate with OrbitPay to re-run their export or we can provide re-export. Closing provisional.
